question: Donald Trump’s threats that the US will now be preventing ships from sailing through the Strait of Hormuz1 are not only manifestly illegal under international law, but they also create a situation in which vessels and crew from EU countries might potentially be attacked by US forces in the area.

If this happens, it is essential for the EU to be ready with a quick and clear response – one that goes beyond the usual empty, bland statements of condemnation. Could the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy therefore please answer the following questions: 1.
What concrete action will the EU take if US forces seek – including by force – to prevent ships from EU countries from sailing through the Strait of Hormuz?

Will US attempts to block EU ships – either through threats or through the actual use of military force – constitute a clear case in which the EU’s anti‑coercion mechanism should be triggered immediately?

Has the Vice-President / High Representative already made it clear to the US and the Trump administration that the threats are illegal and unacceptable and will be met with a response if they are carried out?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.5.2026) The EU will continue to defend the principle of freedom of navigation, in accordance with international law (particularly UN Convention on the Law of the Sea)1. It urges all involved in the conflict to fully ensure a toll-free and safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

The closure of the strait disrupts international trade and threatens global energy and food security. The EU is engaged in the region through operation EU Naval Force ASPIDES ensuring safe passage through the Red Sea. The operation includes the Strait of Hormuz in its area of operation and can help providing security to merchant vessels, once the war ends.
On 30 March 2026, the Council extended the ASPIDES mandate until 28 February 20272.
